prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same root cause: when SSE reconnection in _handle_reconnection exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the client previously just returned silently (the branch was even marked `# pragma: no cover`), leaving the original pending request hanging forever with no error surfaced to the caller. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same root cause: when SSE reconnection in _handle_reconnection exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, the client previously just returned silently (the branch was even marked `# pragma: no cover`), leaving the original pending request hanging forever with no error surfaced to the caller. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2395's diff directly edits the exact MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS bail-out branch and removes its `# pragma: no cover` marker, indicating the failure path is now exercised by a test. It builds the error response from types already used elsewhere in the file (ErrorData, JSONRPCError, INTERNAL_ERROR) and correlates it to the specific waiting request via `ctx.session_message.message.id`, so only the affected request fails rather than the whole connection. PR #3098's diff only adds a generic `_unwrap_exception` helper for pulling a StreamableHTTPError out of an exception tree/group, plus an unrelated `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations` rename; it never shows the bail-out branch itself being touched, so it's a broader, less contained change to exception propagation without the same targeted, test-covered fix at the actual failure site.

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2962 short-circuits the whole block with `has_tool_results and ...`, so a tool_use with no following tool_result no longer raises at all, and its test cites SEP-1577 text explicitly: tool_result MUST be preceded by tool_use, but tool_use has no requirement to be followed by a tool_result. #3053 keeps entering the block and adds `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)`, which still raises for the identical input, just with different wording — the opposite behavior for the same case. The two patches touch identical lines and produce contradictory outcomes (no-error vs. error) for the same scenario, so they cannot both be applied; #2962's behavior matches the cited spec requirement while #3053's 'clarified' error reintroduces the exact failure #2962 is a regression test against.

prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/split logic that could match parameter names as substrings or mis-split on commas inside quoted values; both PRs rewrite the parser as a quote-aware comma tokenizer over the same function in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/split logic that could match parameter names as substrings or mis-split on commas inside quoted values; both PRs rewrite the parser as a quote-aware comma tokenizer over the same function in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma splitter (near-identical state machine logic), but #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which scopes extraction to the Bearer challenge's segment specifically. Per RFC 7235 a WWW-Authenticate header can contain multiple challenges (e.g. Basic and Bearer) in one header value; #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only looks for the first space and treats everything after it as params for a single challenge, which will incorrectly merge params across multiple challenges if more than one scheme is present. #3041's approach handles that case correctly.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote/escape-aware comma splitter (near-identical state machine logic), but #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which scopes extraction to the Bearer challenge's segment specifically. Per RFC 7235 a WWW-Authenticate header can contain multiple challenges (e.g. Basic and Bearer) in one header value; #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only looks for the first space and treats everything after it as params for a single challenge, which will incorrectly merge params across multiple challenges if more than one scheme is present. #3041's approach handles that case correctly.
